method: RGA reports the used VGPR count and numPhysicalVgprs=1024 for every variant. On gfx1030 the allocation granularity is 8 and a wave64 register consumes two of the 1024 wave32-sized slots, so waves per SIMD = 1024 // (2 * ceil(used/8)*8). Wave64 is not assumed: cycle O2 measured SQ_PS WAVES_32 = 0.
argument: Five variants sit at exactly 9 waves per SIMD and span -3.17 % to -41.60 %. The decisive counterexample is `scalar`, which reaches 10 waves per SIMD - MORE occupancy than stack3 - and delivers only -3.84 %, while stack3 at 9 waves delivers -37.49 %. Occupancy therefore cannot be what orders these results.
limits: This is THEORETICAL occupancy derived from register allocation. Achieved occupancy was not measured: the only counter that would have shown it, SQ_PS LEVEL_WAVES, returns an impossible constant on this ASIC (cycle P5). LDS is zero for every variant, so it is not a second limiter here. What this argument establishes is that occupancy does not EXPLAIN the ordering; it does not establish that occupancy contributes nothing to the first few points.
